md: And it was. The letter vav (“and”) adds and connects to where the Torah ended — the account of Moshe’s death: after that the L-rd said to Joshua, etc.
My servant Moshe is dead. That is: had he still been alive, you could not have crossed the Jordan, for it was decreed that he would not cross.
And now. Since he has died — arise, cross, etc.
On which. This goes back to the start of the verse: every spot.
Where the sun sets. That is, on the side where the sun sets — the west.
No one shall stand. That is, no one will find the strength to stand up straight before you.
I will not fail you. I will not withdraw My support from you.
Be strong and resolute. In leading the people properly.
But, etc. For without this, nothing will help you lead the people properly.
That you may. Through keeping the Torah you will succeed.
This. The one spoken of in the previous verse (verse 7): “which Moshe enjoined upon you.”
So that you may observe. For if it departs from your lips, you may forget something.
Only then. When you take care to do, etc. — then you will prosper.
I charge you. I command you: be strong in war against the enemy and do not fear.

For the L-rd is with you, etc. It does not say “for I am with you,” though it was the L-rd Himself who was speaking. So too (I Samuel 12:11): “and He sent… and Shmuel,” though it was Shmuel himself who was speaking.

And charge, etc. Although this is told before the spies were sent, the command must have come after it: on the day the spies went they lodged in Jericho; they stayed three days in the hills; on their return they lodged in their own place; the next day they lodged by the Jordan, and the day after they crossed the Jordan.
Get ready. Although they still ate the manna, they also had produce of the land — what merchants of the nations brought them; this is what he told them to get ready.
Remember. You must remember.
Is granting you a haven. He gives you a place of rest by giving you this land on this side of the Jordan.
Until He grants a haven. Until the L-rd gives a place of rest to them too.
And possess it. That is: then you will hold it with no one disputing it, since you kept the condition.
Where the sun rises. On the eastern side.
Only, etc. That is: we will obey you only when the L-rd is with you, etc., but not otherwise.
Only be strong. To punish the rebels and not to forgive an affront to your honor.
Spies, secretly. To find out what the people were thinking — whether their hearts had melted.
Saying. That is, he said this.
And hid him. Each one in a separate place, for it is easier to hide them one by one.
The men. The ones you are asking about.
But I didn’t know. When they came.
When the gate. That is, when it was time to close the city gate, as it grew dark.
For you can overtake them. Since they left only a short while ago.
And hidden them. She hid them again, in a more hidden place.
Under stalks of flax. Under flax still on its stalks — the stems of the flax.
Laid out. So that no one would notice that someone was hidden there.
After them. So the pursuers thought.
Was shut. Since they wanted to keep searching for them in the city, the gatekeepers shut the gate, so that no one could leave from then on.
They. The spies.
Because dread has fallen, etc. And we have no strength to fight you.
And no spirit was left, etc. That is, everyone’s spirit sank low.
He is G-d. So He has power over them all.
Now. Since the matter is clear.
Loyalty. For you have not yet done me any good.
Show, etc. So you too show kindness to my father’s house, though they did you no good first.
A reliable sign. A true sign — so that all Israel will know not to harm us.
Our persons, etc. If anyone wants to harm you, we will give ourselves up to death to save you.
This mission of ours. The sign you ask for, which will be given to you: if you tell about the sign, many will use it to save themselves.
True loyalty. You did us a kindness but hoped for a reward; we will do you a true kindness, with no hope of reward.
Through the window. Because the city gates were shut.
In the wall. The window faced outward, beyond the city wall.
So that they may not come upon you. If you go your way now, the pursuers may meet you on their way back.
There. In the hills.
Released. That is, we want to be free of the sin of a broken oath, so let us explain the matter well.
We invade. That is, when we come into the land.
This. By which you let us down.
You tie. As a sign and a mark.
Through which. This refers to the window, meaning “by way of it.”
His blood will be on his head. That is, the guilt for his death is on himself — he brought it on himself.
And we shall be clear. For it would have been impossible to keep him from death.
This. This mark and this sign.
Let it be as you say. That is, this is the right way.
She sent them. They went to the hills on her advice, so it says “she sent them.”
And she tied. When Israel came into the land.
Has delivered. The previous verse says that they told all that had happened to them; when they finished telling, they said: here is the conclusion — the L-rd has delivered, etc.
There. By the Jordan.
Three days. As it says above (1:11): “in three days’ time,” etc.
The Ark of the Covenant of the L-rd. The Ark that holds the Tablets: when the L-rd gave them, He made a covenant with Israel.
You shall. Then you shall set out.
Between it. And the Ark.
Some two thousand. Exactly two thousand, since it says “by measure.” The letter kaf (“some”) stresses that it is exact, as in (Genesis 25:31) “sell me this day.”
So that, etc. This goes back to the previous verse: follow the Ark so that you may know the way, since you have never traveled it.
For tomorrow, etc. wonders. So it is fitting to be holy then, and pure of impurity.
So that they shall know. Through the wonders I will do through you.
The edge. Its western edge.
Make a halt in the Jordan. And do not step out onto dry land at once.
By this. By the wonder he goes on to describe.
The Sovereign, etc. That is, “the Ark of the Sovereign,” etc.
Select. So that they, in place of all of you, would stand near the Ark and see that as soon as the priests’ feet came to rest, the waters would be cut off at once.

When the feet come to rest. This goes back to what was said above: they will see that as soon as the priests’ feet come to rest, the water now coming down from upstream will be cut off at once and flow away.
Will stand. The water that comes afterwards to the place where it was cut off will stand there in a single heap.
At its edge. On the eastern side.

The Jordan keeps flowing over its entire bed. This shows how great the miracle was: although the Jordan has much water — even all through the harvest, when rivers usually run low, it was full to its banks.
Piled up. This goes back to what was said above: with all that water, what came down from upstream, after it was cut off, stopped and rose in a single heap.
A great way off. That heap was very far from the town called Adam, which is next to Zarethan.
And those flowing away. The water that flowed down before it was cut off, toward the Sea of the Arabah — the Dead Sea.
Ran out completely. That water ran out of its place entirely and flowed away, and the place was left dry.
Stood. They did not leave the Jordan at once, but stood on the western side until all had crossed, as he had commanded.
Firmly. That is, they stood ready and steady, fixed in place, until all had crossed.
From the middle of the Jordan. He told them to go back to the edge of the Jordan after they had come out of it.
From the spot where they stand. From the place where the priests stood firmly: they lifted their feet, and the men took the stones that were under them.
Whom he had designated. To stand near the Ark and see that as soon as the priests’ feet came to rest, the waters would be cut off, as written above (3:13).
In the middle of the Jordan. For they had already come out of it, as said (verse 1).
A symbol. A sign to remember.
In time to come. That is, after some time.
Twelve, etc. These were other stones (Sotah 35b). “To this day” means forever: whoever reads this verse in his own time says “to this day.” This is an important rule in the words of the prophets.

To convey to the people. Our Sages of blessed memory said (Sotah 34a): G-d commanded him to tell the people, “Know that you are crossing the Jordan on dry land on condition that you drive out all the inhabitants of the land.” And Moshe had commanded him that very thing.
Speedily. Out of respect for the Ark, which stood until they had crossed.
The Ark of the L-rd advanced. After Joshua told the priests to come up out of the Jordan, as written below (verse 17), the Ark crossed over to go before the people.
At the instance of the L-rd. That is, on the mission of the Omnipresent.
And you shall fear. Meaning “and so that you shall fear”: the letter vav is missing, and there are many such cases.
And no spirit was left, etc. Said as an overstatement: as if the spirit of life had left them from their great fear.
A second circumcision, etc. It says “second” because on the night they left Egypt, too, all Israel was circumcised together; so said our Sages of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah 11:6).
At Gibeath. At the Hill of Foreskins; the place was named after what happened there.
This is the reason. That is, this is why Joshua alone circumcised the whole people, and they did not circumcise one another then: how could it be that none of them knew how to circumcise?
All the people. That is, all the people who came out of Egypt — who were circumcised and fit to circumcise others — had died in the wilderness, and none were left to circumcise the rest.
Had been circumcised. That is, only the people who came out were circumcised, but not those born in the wilderness, so they were not fit to circumcise others.
Until the entire nation had perished, etc. So none of the circumcised was left who was fit and suited to circumcise others.
Had sworn. Because of this the L-rd swore to them that they would not, etc.
He had raised up in their stead. That is, “whom He had raised up in their stead.”

These Joshua circumcised. They had not been circumcised until then — they were uncircumcised up to that time, for those who came out of Egypt did not circumcise their sons on the way. So apart from Joshua there was no circumcised man fit and suited to circumcise others.

Today I have rolled away. Now I have removed from you the taunt of the Egyptians, who said, “Why, they are uncircumcised like us!” For Israel this is a disgrace, as it is written (Genesis 34:14): “for that is a disgrace to us.”
Toward evening. After midday it is called “evening,” for then the sun inclines toward the west.
On the day after the passover. On the day after the first day of Pesach, which is the time of bringing the Omer: they brought the Omer and then ate.

The manna ceased. Although the manna stopped falling on the day Moshe died, the seventh of Adar, they were miraculously fed from the manna left in their vessels; once they ate of the produce of the land, they found no more of it.
They ate. They began to eat.
Near Jericho. That is, within the bounds of Jericho.
Are you one of us. The letter hei here asks a question: have you come to help us against the enemy, or to help the enemy?

He replied, “No.” That is: I have not come to help Israel’s enemies, for I am the captain of Israel, who are called the L-rd’s host. And you have not seen me until now because I have come only now, and not before.
What does my lord command. That is: say your words and I am ready to carry them out, as a servant carries out his master’s words.
Is holy. And it is fitting to stand on it barefoot.

Shut up tight. That is, it had always been closed with doors and bolt, and now they closed it even more because of Israel and let no one leave or enter, so that the ways into the city would not become known.
Warriors. That is, even though they are mighty warriors.
Do this. Go around once a day.
Blowing. Every day, when they go around.
That sound. That is, the sound drawn out in a long blast.
Every man straight ahead. They will not need to go around and climb it, for the whole wall will fall.
When Joshua had instructed. That is, they did just as Joshua told the people, and the seven, etc.
Blowing the horns. This refers to the priests.
Sounding all the time. That is, the priests did not stand still while blowing, but walked and blew.
Rose early. On the second day.
Blowing as they marched. Repeated to say that they never stopped blowing.
At daybreak. So that there would be enough time to go around seven times.
Only, etc. That is why they had to rise earlier then than on the other days.
Blew. That is, a drawn-out, long blast.
Proscribed. For destruction and cutting off.
It, etc. That is, the city itself and whatever in it is not fit to be brought into the treasury of the L-rd.
For the L-rd. That is, for the sake of the L-rd’s name and His honor.
Beware. Guard yourselves and others from taking anything of what is proscribed.
Or else you will be proscribed, if you take, etc. Lest you cut off Israel by what you take of the proscribed, for all would perish; this is “you will cause the camp to be proscribed,” etc.
All the silver, etc. These are the things fit for the treasury of the L-rd.
So the people shouted. And it goes on to explain: when the people heard the sound of the horn — when it is drawn out in a long blast — then they shouted.
Pronounced this oath. A curse is called an oath.

He shall lay its foundations at the cost of his first-born. When he lays the foundation, his firstborn son will die; the rest will die while the building goes on; and when he sets up the gates, his youngest son will die. So all of them will die.
Violated, etc. Because they did not watch over one another, Scripture counts it as if all of them had violated it.
Not all need go up. That is, there is no need for all of them.
If only we had been content. Had we only wanted then to stay on the eastern side of the Jordan and not cross the Jordan, this trouble would not have come upon us.
What can I say. Sensing that he had said too much against the L-rd’s deed, he spoke again: what can I say if not this, since Israel has turned tail in flight? And I cry out from the pain of my heart.
Will hear. That the enemy is pursuing them.
And what will You do about Your name. So that it will not be profaned when they say, “They perished because the L-rd was unable.”
Why, etc. That is, there is no need for prayer, only to remove the one who violated the proscription.
Israel has sinned. Although one man sinned, still, because they did not watch over one another, Scripture counts it as if all of them had sinned.

They have broken My covenant. This comes to stress how great that outrage was: even one who sins against another person will not go unpunished, and they did not fear and broke My covenant — they violated the proscription, which is like an oath.
They have taken. That is, even one who transgresses any other of the L-rd's commandments will surely be punished, and they even took from what was consecrated to the Most High, the L-rd's portion.

They have stolen. Had they taken it in front of everyone, they would at least have treated the honor of the Omnipresent like the honor of a human being of flesh and blood; but they stole, hiding from people, and did not fear the L-rd.
They have broken faith. A thief is not despised if he repents, confesses and returns what he took, but they even denied it.

And put it in their vessels. That is (Proverbs 6:30): “A thief is not despised for stealing to appease his hunger,” but they even put it in their vessels to keep it as treasure, not to use it to satisfy their hunger. So that outrage was double and many times over.
For they have become proscribed. That is, they helped the one who violated the proscription by looking away and not watching over one another.
What is proscribed. The one who violated the proscription.
Purify yourselves. To pass before the Ark, to find out on whose account this trouble came.
You shall present yourselves. Before the Ark.
By tribes. Each tribe separately.
That the L-rd indicates (lit. “captures”). It will be “captured” before the Ark, so that for a while it cannot move from its place.
Shall come forward by clans. After they are moved from their place, they will come forward again by clans.
By ancestral houses. For the clan is further divided into ancestral houses.
Man by man. Individual men.
He who is indicated for proscription. The one who is “captured” before the Ark because he misappropriated the proscribed.
The clans of Judah. The tribe, too, is called a clan.
Man by man. Each man the head of an ancestral house.
And Zabdi was indicated. He was the head of the ancestral house.
Man by man. Individual men.
Honor to the L-rd. For when they see that you were indicated justly, it will be honor to the L-rd.
And make confession to Him. Admit that it is true that you misappropriated the proscribed.
What you have done. That is, what things you took from the proscribed.

This is what I did (lit. “like this and like this”). Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 42b) that he said: I did this before, too — something like this in the war against the Canaanite and in the war against Midian; for in the war against the Canaanite, too, it is said (Numbers 21:2): “I will proscribe their towns,” and in Midian, too, they gave the gold as holy to the L-rd.
They are. The mantle and the wedge of gold.
Under it. Under the mantle.
Who hurried. So that Achan's relatives would not take the things to cover up their disgrace.
And displayed them. That is, they spread them out before the Ark, so that everyone would see that it was true.
With him. They went with Joshua.

And brought them up. Although they went to a valley, it says “brought up,” for before they reached the valley they went up by a mountain road to the valley, which was called “the Valley of Achor” (“of calamity”) after what happened.
What calamity you have brought upon us. That is, what great calamity you have brought upon us — and for this the L-rd will bring calamity upon you.

And stoned them. His sons and daughters and his ox, etc. (Perhaps because his sons and daughters knew of it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 44a), and did not reveal it, they too were stoned. However, our Sages, of blessed memory, did not say so.)
They put them to the fire. The mantle, the wedge and the tent, etc.
Over him. Over his grave.
Which is still there. That is, it stands forever in its size.
That is why, etc., as is still the case. That is, it still has that name.
Do not be frightened. Since they had already fallen at this place, he was afraid to approach it again; therefore He told him, “Do not be frightened.”

All the fighting troops. He commanded that all these preparations and stratagems be made to mislead the nations, so that they would think that the whole victory came from the size of the army and the stratagems, and not that the hand of the L-rd had done this. Because of this they would all gather together, so that they too would be a large army and could devise plans and stratagems with many advisers. And this would be good for Israel, for they would strike them all at once, without needing to go from city to city to strike them.
Behind it. Not from the side from which you will approach it.
On the alert. To move quickly when needed.
We will flee. In order to mislead them.
They will come. And then they will come out to pursue us.
Until we have drawn them. That is, the flight will help until we draw them away from the city to pursue us, for they will say that we are really fleeing out of fear, as in the first battle.
While we are fleeing. And we will keep on fleeing, to draw them away from the city.
From your ambush. From the place where you will lie in ambush.
The city. Those who remain in the city.
As the L-rd has commanded. Who commanded that it be burned, as is written above (verse 2): “You shall treat Ai as you treated Jericho.”
Mind, I have given you your orders. That is, be careful and do not disobey my word.
Mustered. He checked whether they were ready for battle.
And stationed them as an ambush. He set yet another ambush, closer to the city.
Thus the army was disposed. The people themselves prepared the camp for battle, etc., and also prepared its far end — that is the ambush.
In the valley. To come closer to the city.
To the meeting place (lit. “to the appointed time”). At the same time at which they had gone out in the first battle.
As though routed. They made themselves look as if they were “stricken,” that is, beaten and weakened.
Gathered. They gathered at the call of the one who summoned them.
Hold out the javelin. To give a sign to the ambush to come into the city.
The pursuers. These are the men of Ai, who at first had been pursuing Israel.
The other. The men of the ambush.
And put it to the sword. The women and children.

A copy of the Teaching of Moses. The book “These are the words” (Deuteronomy) is called “Mishneh Torah” (the Repetition of the Torah), for in it is said a second time what was said in the four books before it.
Facing the levitical priests. The priests, sons of Levi, who stood with the Ark in the middle and said the blessing and the curse.
Half of them. Six tribes.

To bless, etc., of old (lit. “first”). (Mishnah, Sotah 7:5): First they began and said, “Blessed is the man who does not make a sculptured image, etc.,” and after this they said, “Cursed is the man, etc.,” and so with all the curses.
He read. Joshua was the one who read, as is written in the next verse.

All the words of the Teaching. And it goes on to explain that he read the blessing and the curse, just as is written in the Torah: these are the passages (Deuteronomy 28:1) “If you obey…” and “If you do not obey…,” said in the portion Ki Tavo, and others like them.
There was not a word. Of the blessing and the curse.
That Moses had commanded. That is, what is said in the Torah.
